name.en: TAN (Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number) Registration

authority: Income Tax Department, Ministry of Finance, Government of India

description.en: TAN (Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number) is a 10-character alphanumeric number issued by the Income Tax Department to persons who are required to deduct or collect tax at source (TDS/TCS). All persons responsible for deducting or collecting tax at source under the Income Tax Act, 1961 are required to apply for and obtain TAN.

verifiedConditions.appliesTo: Persons required to deduct tax at source under Income Tax Act
verifiedConditions.claim: Any person who is required to deduct tax at source (TDS) under the provisions of the Income Tax Act, 1961 must apply for and obtain a TAN. This includes employers deducting TDS on salaries, businesses deducting TDS on contractor payments, and others specified under Sections 192 to 206C.

verifiedConditions.appliesTo: Persons required to collect tax at source under Income Tax Act
verifiedConditions.claim: Any person who is required to collect tax at source (TCS) under Section 206C of the Income Tax Act, 1961 must obtain a TAN. This includes sellers of specified goods like timber, minerals, scrap, and motor vehicles above prescribed thresholds.

unverifiedEligibility: Government deductors may have a separate process for TAN allotment through the Accounts Officer.
A person can hold only one TAN for the same category of tax deduction responsibility; multiple TANs for the same entity are not permitted.
TAN is not required for individuals or entities that have no TDS or TCS obligations.

requirements.claim: Form 49B is the prescribed application form for allotment of TAN. It requires details of the applicant including name, address, category of deductor, PAN, and nature of TDS/TCS responsibility.
PAN (Permanent Account Number) of the deductor or collector is required in the TAN application. The PAN helps link TDS/TCS deductions to the correct entity.
Proof of identity of the applicant such as Aadhaar, Voter ID, Passport, or company registration certificate for corporate applicants.
Proof of address of the deductor such as electricity bill, bank statement, registered office address proof, or lease agreement.

processInformation.appliesTo: All TAN applicants using online method
processInformation.claim: Visit the TIN-NSDL website (tin-nsdl.com) or the new Income Tax e-filing portal. Select 'Apply Online for TAN' and fill Form 49B with the required details including name, address, category of deductor, and PAN.

Select the appropriate category of deductor from the list: Central Government, State Government, Company, Branch/Division of a Company, Firm, Trust, Association of Persons, Body of Individuals, Local Authority, Individual, or Artificial Juridical Person.
Pay the processing fee of Rs. 65 (plus applicable taxes) through the online payment gateway using net banking, debit card, credit card, or demand draft.

Upon successful submission and payment, a 14-digit acknowledgment number is generated. For online applications, the signed acknowledgment must be sent to NSDL e-Governance Infrastructure Limited, Pune within 15 days of online application.
NSDL processes the application and forwards it to the Income Tax Department for TAN allotment. Upon allotment, the TAN is communicated to the applicant via email and post.

output.claim: A TAN Allotment Letter is issued containing the 10-character alphanumeric TAN in the format AAAA99999A (4 letters, 5 digits, 1 letter). The TAN must be quoted in all TDS/TCS returns, challans, certificates, and correspondence with the Income Tax Department.

fees.applicability: TAN application processing fee payable to NSDL
fees.claim: The processing fee for TAN application (Form 49B) is Rs. 65 plus applicable Goods and Services Tax. This fee is payable at the time of application submission.

processingTime.applicability: TAN allotment processing time from date of receipt of complete application
processingTime.claim: TAN allotment typically takes 7-15 working days from the date of receipt of the complete and valid application by NSDL. Online applications are generally processed faster than offline applications.

sources.title: Income Tax Department — TAN Information
sources.publisher: Income Tax Department, Central Board of Direct Taxes, Ministry of Finance, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: The Income Tax Department portal provides information on TAN requirements, the obligation to obtain TAN for TDS/TCS deductors, and the legal provisions under the Income Tax Act, 1961 governing TAN.
claimsSupported: TAN is mandatory for all persons responsible for TDS or TCS.
PAN of the deductor is required.
TAN must be quoted in all TDS/TCS returns and challans.
sources.uncertainty: The Income Tax e-filing portal is being updated; some features may migrate between the old and new portals.

sources.title: TIN-NSDL — TAN Application Services
sources.publisher: NSDL e-Governance Infrastructure Limited (authorized by Income Tax Department)
sources.evidenceExcerpt: TIN-NSDL is the authorized agency for processing TAN applications. The portal provides online and offline TAN application facility through Form 49B, fee payment, and status tracking.
claimsSupported: Online TAN application through Form 49B is available.
Processing fee is Rs. 65 plus GST.
Category of deductor must be selected during application.
Identity proof and address proof are required.
sources.uncertainty: NSDL is an intermediary; final TAN allotment is by the Income Tax Department.

limitations: This record covers new TAN allotment only; TAN change/correction (Form 49B for changes) is not covered.
The specific TDS/TCS sections and thresholds that trigger TAN obligation are not fully enumerated.
Government deductors may have a separate process through the Pay and Accounts Officer (PAO) which is not covered.
The record does not cover TAN cancellation or surrender processes.
Penalty provisions under Section 272BB for failure to obtain or quoting incorrect TAN are not covered.

review.reviewReason: Core TAN registration process is reviewed, but comprehensive TDS/TCS obligation thresholds and government deductor procedures are not fully modeled.
